validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The gem.wiki page's ONLY citation is OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2017, p.134. That live opec.org PDF link has ROTTED (now returns the OPEC site homepage HTML, not the PDF). I retrieved the genuine PDF from the Wayback Machine (snapshot 2025-02-06) and read it directly: Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016' lists, under Iraq, a row 'Trans-Iraqi dry gas pipeline/Dewania | OPC | 50 | 24'. The column headers are explicitly 'Length (miles)' and 'Diameter (inches)'. So the pipeline is named and spec'd specifically (not a generic/aggregate citation) by an official, non-GEM source -> existence adequately supported by ONE authoritative source. I could NOT find any second independent source (English or Arabic) that names this Dewania gas branch; web searches for the line and its specs returned nothing specific. Corroboration is therefore single-source -> tier MEDIUM, not high. CLASSIFICATION: OPEC calls it a 'dry gas pipeline' branch, i.e. gas transmission -> GEM Fuel='Gas' and the gas-tracker placement are CORRECT. It is NOT one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines (none of those match a Diwaniyah gas branch). Not a plant-internal or gathering line. DUPLICATE: distinct from its Trans-Iraqi siblings - P4062 Hilla (OPEC 'Branch from Trans-Iraq dry gas pipeline/Hilla-2 PWR St', 25/24), P4064 Najaf ('/Najaf PWR St', 74/24), P4066 Daura ('/Daura PWR St', 29/18). P4065 = the '/Dewania' entry (50/24), a separate row in the same OPEC table; NOT a relabel/segment double-count. SPEC: LengthKnown 50 mi and units 'mi' EXACTLY match OPEC (50 miles); Diameter 24 in EXACTLY matches; Fuel gas matches ('dry gas'). Capacity is blank and OPEC gives no capacity - left blank (see fills, UNRESOLVED). ATTRIBUTION: GEM Owner1='Iraq Ministry of Oil' (100%); OPEC lists the operator as OPC (Oil Pipelines Company / State Company for Oil Pipelines), a state entity under the Ministry of Oil - so the owner is defensible but the precise operator (OPC) is missing; recommend adding OPC as operator. STATUS: OPEC 2016 data-year lists it among operating main gas pipelines; the Diwaniyah power plant is gas-fired (power-technology.com), consistent with a live gas feed. No post-2016 source re-confirms it, so 'operating' rests on the 2016 snapshot - caveat, not a concern.

fills.researcher_notes: Sheet endpoints were bare (start=Iraq, end=Iraq). OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 gives the connection as 'Trans-Iraqi dry gas pipeline/Dewania': start = a tap on the Trans-Iraq dry-gas trunk, end = Dewania/Diwaniyah in Al-Qadisiyah province. The Wayback OPEC PDF 200s but its token cannot be substring-matched by the verifier because it is a binary PDF (contains_value=false); I confirmed the exact table line offline via pdftotext. Wikipedia and database.earth verify Diwaniyah is in Al-Qadisiyah Governorate, Iraq (city 31.9929N, 44.9255E). End is very likely the Al-Diwaniyah gas-fired power plant (siblings all feed 'PWR St'), but OPEC wrote only 'Dewania' so I did not assert the plant as a hard value.

Capacity is blank in GEM. OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 gives only length and diameter (no throughput), and no independent source states a capacity for this Dewania branch. Not forcing a number onto a weak field - left blank.

routes.start_name: Tap-off on the Trans-Iraq dry gas pipeline (main dry-gas trunk)
routes.corridor_desc: A 50-mile (~80 km) 24-inch branch off the Trans-Iraq dry gas pipeline delivering gas to Diwaniyah in Al-Qadisiyah province, south-central Iraq (mid-Euphrates corridor). The delivery end is well established (Diwaniyah city / its gas-fired power plant, ~31.99N, 44.93E). The START is only loosely bounded: it is a tap on the Trans-Iraq dry-gas trunk roughly 80 km from Diwaniyah, but neither OPEC nor any other source I found gives the tap coordinates or the trunk's exact alignment near Qadisiyah, so the tap could lie south toward the Samawah/Rumaythah reach or north toward the Hilla/Najaf reach of the trunk. I did NOT invent a start coordinate (left null). Tight corridor: end fixed at Diwaniyah; start within ~80 km along the Trans-Iraq trunk.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint established from OPEC's connection string 'Trans-Iraqi dry gas pipeline/Dewania' + Diwaniyah geolocation (database.earth: 31.99289N, 44.92552E; Wikipedia: Al-Qadisiyah Governorate, Iraq). power-technology confirms Diwaniyah hosts a gas-fired (CCGT) power plant, consistent with the branch's delivery purpose. End coordinate is the Diwaniyah city center anchor (plant sits on the city outskirts); I did not claim plant-exact coordinates. Start/tap coordinate left null - not sourced, not fabricated. Route accuracy 'low': one endpoint fixed, other end and alignment unresolved.

summary: P4065 Trans-Iraqi-Dewania is real and correctly a gas branch (OPEC ASB 2017 Table 9.9 names it: 50 mi / 24 in, OPC) - confirmed (caveat): single-source only (that lone gem.wiki citation is link-rotted; recovered via Wayback), owner should add operator OPC, endpoints were blank; suggested route accuracy low.
